August 8, 1998
POT HARVEST NETS 24,000 PLANTS

Drug Agents, National Guard Attack Marijuana

MADISON, Posted 6:05 p.m. August 8, 1998 --The Dane County Narcotics and Gang Task Force, along with members of the National Guard, spent this morning destroying thousands of wild marijuana plants.

The task force destroyed about 24,000 wild marijuana plants today, so people won’t find the plants and try to use for illegal purposes, WISC-TV reported.

Area farmers cultivated the hemp to use in military supplies during World War I and II. Remnants of these war efforts remain today—in one case as an entire marijuana-covered hillside on a western Dane County farm.

It was a sight, and a mission, National Guard member Nathan Olson hardly expected to be part of.

"We had no idea—we were told to come to the armory at 7 (a.m.) and divide up the Humvees," Olson told WISC-TV. "We just got briefed this morning, we really didn’t know."

Eradicating the drug is a service that’s helping the war against drugs.

"I have nieces and nephews and I don’t want getting into this," National Guard member Melissa Breihan said. "It’s helping out everybody."

Law enforcement officers said the Guard’s help is much appreciated.

"Having a larger group of people doing a coordinated effort just allows us to get through the areas faster," Sgt. Mark Twombly, left, told WISC-TV.

"We’ll probably be out next summer doing the same thing," Twombly said.

The plants will be burned at an undisclosed location.
